title: Linear-size sample compression
formal: Is there a universal integer \(C\ge1\) such that every nonempty Boolean concept class \(H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}\) on an arbitrary set \(X\), with finite VC dimension \(d\ge1\), admits a labeled sample compression scheme with nonnegative integer kernel and side-information bounds \(k,b\) satisfying \[k+b\le Cd?\] The scheme is exact on every finite \(H\)-realizable sample, stores an unordered subset of labeled sample records plus \(b\) bits, and may reconstruct a predictor outside \(H\). Its compressor, reconstructor, \(k\), and \(b\) may depend on the complete class, but the same scheme and bounds must work for all sample sizes. Only \(C\) must be universal. This preserves the card’s previously selected linear-size, counted-side-information formulation.
definitions: A concept is a total Boolean function on \(X\). A finite set \(U\subseteq X\) is shattered by \(H\) if \(\{h|_U:h\in H\}=\{0,1\}^{U}\); the VC dimension is the largest cardinality of a shattered set. A finite labeled sample is a finite set \(S\subseteq X\times\{0,1\}\). It is \(H\)-realizable if some \(h\in H\) agrees with every pair in \(S\); in particular, a realizable sample has no contradictory labels at the same point. The empty sample is allowed. A scheme consists of deterministic set maps \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\). For every realizable \(S\), \(\kappa(S)=(T,z)\), where \(T\subseteq S\), \(|T|\le k\), and \(z\in\{0,1\}^{b}\). The reconstruction \(\rho(T,z):X\to\{0,1\}\) is a total predictor satisfying \[\rho(\kappa(S))(x)=y\qquad\text{for every }(x,y)\in S.\] The reconstructor is defined for all possible finite labeled kernels of size at most \(k\) and all \(b\)-bit strings, with consistency required only on actual compressed messages. It receives no original sample, sample size, omitted point, original index or ordering of retained examples. One retained labeled example costs one unit, even on a domain whose points have no finite binary descriptions; each side-information bit costs one unit. The retained set is unordered. A finite side alphabet \(I\) instead of bit strings costs \(\lceil\log_2|I|\rceil\) bits. Allowing variable-length strings of bounded length changes this linear-size question only by a constant factor if their lengths are encoded as part of the message. The compressor is required only on realizable samples. Reconstruction need not be proper, stable under deletion of unused records, computable, efficient, or measurable. No randomness or data-distribution promise is involved. Dimension zero is omitted from the display because a nonempty such class has one pointwise labeling and admits a scheme storing nothing. All classes of positive finite dimension, not just finite domains or finite classes, are included.
answer_criterion: Give a Lean-checked proof of the stated universal linear bound, or of its logical negation. A positive answer must provide a single universal constant and, for each class, a valid compressor and reconstructor with the counted size bound holding on every realizable sample. A negative answer must show that for every integer \(C\ge1\), some class of positive finite VC dimension admits no such scheme of size at most \(Cd\). A lower bound against only proper, stable, efficient, or otherwise restricted reconstruction does not refute this unrestricted target. Neither does failure of a particular embedding construction. Free side information or free ordering of retained points is outside the model. The requirement is exact consistency and linear size with a universal constant; it asks for no additive numerical approximation.
why: A central question connecting the combinatorial complexity of prediction with how many observations suffice to represent all training decisions. Its universality across concept classes, and its links to learning, extremal set systems and graph geometry, make the linear-versus-exponential gap fundamental.

importance.reason: A longstanding general conjecture asking whether VC dimension controls sample representation up to a constant factor; it reaches far beyond any one learning algorithm or geometric example.

progress.text: The framework of Littlestone and Warmuth led to the conjecture that compression size can be linear in VC dimension; the general conjecture remains explicit in the 2025 survey of reductions.
Moran and Yehudayoff prove a general \(2^{O(d)}\) bound for binary classes. The corrected arXiv v2 is the appropriate preprint; the journal version appeared in JACM in 2016.
Chase and coauthors prove an exponential dimension obstruction to embedding arbitrary VC classes in extremal classes, limiting a major proposed approach without refuting sample compression itself.
Bourneuf and coauthors obtain almost-linear proper compression in treewidth and cliquewidth for graph-ball classes, while retaining the general conjecture as open.

The latest version of arXiv:2603.23561, which had earlier claimed a compression breakthrough and later a no-clash teaching result, is withdrawn. Its authors identify an incorrect proof of Lemma 2. This is not a resolution.

Rechecked the unordered-kernel and side-information models, the 2016 theorem, the 2024 embedding obstruction, the April 2026 structured results and the current withdrawal notice. A bounded later-work search found no matching general linear bound or counterexample.

status_note: Checked through 16 September 2026. The April 2026 primary graph-ball paper explicitly retains the general linear conjecture; its structured width-dependent results and the 2024 embedding obstruction do not settle this target. arXiv:2603.23561v4 remains withdrawn, with an incorrect Lemma 2 proof identified by the authors. A bounded later-work search found no matching resolution. The model retains unordered labeled subsets and counted side bits, with no computational or properness restriction.

context_blocks.text: The compressed object lets a fixed decoder reproduce every label in the original training sample. It need not identify the unknown target on points that were never observed. The same decoder must work at every sample size, so a bound depending only on the class’s VC dimension would be independent of how much training data was supplied.

The distinction between examples and bits is essential. A domain point may require arbitrarily many bits to describe, but sample compression charges one unit for retaining its labeled record. Conversely, an unbounded uncharged message would evade the intended resource bound. Both the retained kernel and the side information are therefore limited explicitly, and the kernel has no free ordering.

Moran and Yehudayoff prove that every binary class of VC dimension \(d\) has a scheme of total size \(2^{O(d)}\). Their sharper theorem also depends on dual VC dimension, which exchanges the roles of domain points and hypotheses by regarding a point as its vector of labels across the class. That dual dimension can grow exponentially in \(d\), leaving the general linear-versus-exponential gap. The checked result is from the corrected v2 and subsequent journal publication.

Chase and coauthors show that some finite classes require an exponential increase in dimension to be contained in an extremal class, a structured type of class with known tight compression. This limits a previously studied embedding-based route to compression. It does not prove that the original class itself requires an exponential-size scheme.

The April 2026 graph-ball paper explicitly retains the general linear conjecture. It gives proper compression of size \(O(t\log(t+1))\) for graph-ball classes whose underlying graph has treewidth at most \(t\), and an analogous cliquewidth result. The predictors are themselves balls, but the resource parameter is graph width and the family is restricted. These structured results are not a universal linear-VC theorem.

The 2025 reduction paper transfers some binary compression bounds to multiclass, regression and robust-learning settings. The sharper transfers need additional reconstruction or stability properties. The ordinary linear conjecture appears in its introduction; its later robust-compression open problem is a different target.

A March 2026 preprint first claimed a sample-compression breakthrough and later a no-clash teaching result. The current checked version, dated 3 August 2026, is withdrawn and identifies an incorrect proof of Lemma 2. Its stale search-result title and earlier abstract are not evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.

sentences: Sample compression keeps labeled examples and a short side message from which a fixed decoder recovers every original training label.
The conjecture asks for a bound linear in VC dimension, uniformly across all Boolean concept classes.
This card counts both retained examples and side bits, and permits arbitrary predictors and unlimited computation.
The general known upper bound is exponential, while recent structured results and an embedding obstruction do not close that gap.
A complete Lean answer must prove the universal linear bound or rule it out for some classes, and the withdrawn 2026 claim supplies no resolution.
